The m90 supplements showed that ordinary low and intermediate points can be close while the severe pyridyl failures persist at selected weak-eluent conditions, so I retained a focused azaaromatic curve rather than applying a universal late-retention correction. The m159 curve was more structured than the original extreme prediction: 79ff49052bce33597828, cfcf2b8c54d4c8b3838a, and 8cbab5e832e82452994c were close, while 1395836aef00d6a880b0 modestly overpredicted the high-ratio tail. I therefore selected one intermediate high-ratio point and one lower-ratio loading contrast. The m211 results were accurate at an intermediate ratio but overpredicted several early points, reinforcing the need to distinguish graph and regime effects. For m216, d1e71a8278523e7a10e3 was accurate while ae187d6f3746213b630c underpredicted V2, so the new points target endpoint shape and loading. The m92 EA outcomes showed mixed V2 direction across 10/1 and 2/1 conditions, which supports measuring a compact EA response curve rather than assuming a monotone solvent shift. The large m11, m99, m119, acid, and multifunctional endpoint errors keep V2-tail repair central to this round.","batch_rationale":"The batch combines local response curves with cross-family controls. m90, m159, m11, m216, and m141 target ratio-dependent basic or nitrile regimes where the measured trajectory contains both accurate boundary rows and severe late failures. m92 supplies three EA-loaded points to isolate loading-solvent effects. m119, m99, m88, m37, m94, m72, m205, m204, m193, and m45 target endpoint-width and loading failures that recur across donor-rich, acidic, multifunctional, and aromatic families. m182, m40, m78, and m123 provide neutral or weakly polar controls so corrections learned from polar structures do not transfer indiscriminately. The selected pairs and small curves should improve generalization by teaching condition-response boundaries, loading interactions, and V2 endpoint shape across chemical regions represented in the Row-distribution."}
